title: Grothendieck spectral sequence
statement:
Let $(F,G)$ be a composable pair [def-sp-composite-acyclicity] with $F$
sending injectives to $G$-acyclics. For every $X\in\mathcal A$ there is a
functorial first-quadrant spectral sequence whose $E_2$-page is

$$
 E_2^{p,q}=R^pG\bigl(R^qF(X)\bigr)
$$

and which converges to $R^{p+q}(G\circ F)(X)$; its edge maps in degree $n$
have directions $R^nG(F(X))\to R^n(G\circ F)(X)\to G(R^nF(X))$, and the
spectral sequence depends functorially on $X$. \emph{Construction (part of the statement).} The spectral sequence is the one obtained as follows: choose an injective resolution $X\to J^\bullet$ in $\mathcal A$ and a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution $F(J^\bullet)\to I^{\bullet,\bullet}$ of the complex $F(J^\bullet)$ (a first-quadrant double complex of injectives whose columns $I^{p,\bullet}$ resolve $F(J^p)$ and whose rows of boundaries, cycles and cohomology objects are injective resolutions of those of $F(J^\bullet)$); the spectral sequence of the theorem is the second spectral sequence (the one of the filtration by the resolution degree of $I^{\bullet,\bullet}$, whose $E_1$-term is horizontal cohomology of $G(I^{\bullet,q})$ and whose $E_2$-term is $R^qG$ of the cohomology of $F(J^\bullet)$) of the double complex $G(I^{\bullet,\bullet})$ in the sense of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences], [def-sp-double-complex-total], whose total complex computes $R(G\circ F)(X)$ because $F$ sends injectives to $G$-acyclics; the $E_2$-identification and the abutment are the ones this construction gives.

external.place: (*References: Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Theorem 5.8.3;

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $X\to J^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], so $R^nF(X)=H^n(F(J^\bullet))$ and $R^n(G\circ F)(X)=H^n(GF(J^\bullet))$ for this choice by [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. Since $F$ is additive by [def-sp-composite-acyclicity], $K^\bullet=F(J^\bullet)$ is a nonnegative cochain complex. The category $\mathcal B$ has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], so [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists] gives a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution $K^\bullet\to I^{\bullet,\bullet}$ whose columns $I^{p,\bullet}$ resolve $K^p$.

Put $D^{p,q}=G(I^{p,q})$. By [def-sp-double-complex-total] it has a finite direct-sum total complex with two filtrations. [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] gives both spectral sequences and their common abutment $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$. For the filtration by the original complex degree $p$, its first page is $H^q(G(I^{p,\bullet}))=R^qG(K^p)$, since the column is an injective resolution by [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists] and $R^qG$ is computed on such a resolution by [def-sp-left-exact-additive] and [lem-sp-derived-well-defined].

The first page of Step 2 is zero for $q>0$ by the acyclicity in [def-sp-composite-acyclicity]. In degree $q=0$ it is $GF(J^p)$ because $R^0G=G$ by [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. Its horizontal differential is induced by $J^\bullet$, so its second page is $H^p(GF(J^\bullet))=R^p(G\circ F)(X)$ by Step 1, and vanishes for $q>0$. The first-quadrant stabilization and the finite filtration with $\operatorname{gr}^pH^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$ of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] are the convergence hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-first-quadrant-row-collapse], which then gives $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)\cong E_2^{n,0}=R^n(G\circ F)(X)$.

source.place: Lemma 015N, proof: acyclic collapse and abutment

proof.text: For the filtration by resolution degree $q$, [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] gives $E_1^{q,p}=H^p_I(G(I^{\bullet,q}))$. By [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists], horizontal cycles and boundaries in each row are injective, so [lem-sp-cart-eilenberg-left-exact-cohomology] applied to that row gives $H^p_I(G(I^{\bullet,q}))\cong G(H^p_I(I^{\bullet,q}))$. The complex in $q$ of $H^p_I(I^{\bullet,q})$ is an injective resolution of $H^p(F(J^\bullet))$, again by [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists]. Thus [def-sp-left-exact-additive] and [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], with $H^p(F(J^\bullet))=R^pF(X)$ from Step 1, identify the next page, after index relabeling $(q,p)\mapsto(p,q)$, with $R^pG(R^qF(X))$. The common-abutment clause of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] and Step 3 give convergence to $R^{p+q}(G\circ F)(X)$.

source.place: Definition 015H, Lemma 015I, and Lemma 015N, proof: derived E2 page

proof.text: The first-quadrant finite image filtration and $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}$ are stated by [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] and [def-sp-convergence]. No differential leaves the bottom position $(n,0)$ on pages $r\geq2$, and none enters the left position $(0,n)$. The page-to-page quotient at the bottom gives $E_2^{n,0}\twoheadrightarrow E_\infty^{n,0}=F^nH^n\hookrightarrow H^n$; the left edge is $H^n\twoheadrightarrow H^n/F^1H^n=E_\infty^{0,n}\hookrightarrow E_2^{0,n}$. Using the identifications of Steps 3-4 and $R^0F=F$, $R^0G=G$ from [lem-sp-derived-well-defined] gives exactly the two directions in the statement.

source.place: Lemma 015N, proof: finite filtration and edge maps

proof.text: For $f:X\to Y$, lift $f$ to a map of injective resolutions $J_X^\bullet\to J_Y^\bullet$ by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists], apply $F$, and use [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-eilenberg-functorial] with the identity exact functor of $\mathcal B$ to lift the resulting complex map to a map of Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions. The cited lemma is stated with the two indices exchanged; it gives a morphism of double complexes, and a morphism of double complexes preserves both degree filtrations of [def-sp-double-complex-total], in particular the one by resolution degree, so it gives a filtered map of total complexes, so [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] gives compatible maps of spectral sequences. Comparison homotopies make these maps independent of the chosen lifts from the second page onward; this independence is [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-comparison-independence]. Hence the page, abutment and edge identifications are natural in $X$.
